newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: UAE leader swears in new cabinet led by same PM.
newsitem.headline: UAE leader swears in new cabinet led by same PM.

text.p: United Arab Emirates President Sheikh Zaid bin Sultan al-Nahayan on Sunday swore in a new government led by the same prime minister, Sheikh Maktoum bin Rashid al-Maktoum, the official WAM news agency said.

In a reshuffle last Tuesday he appointed a new oil minister, Obaid bin Saif al-Nasseri, and a new information minister, his son, Sheikh Abdullah bin Zaid al-Nahayan, but re-appointed the ministers of defence, foreign affairs and finance.
Sheikh Zaid instructed the government to support the Palestinian people until they "regained all their rights on their land and soil," WAM said.
He said there would be no Arab-Israeli peace without the return of Arab (East) Jerusalem, seized from Jordan during the 1967 war.

"The challenges facing the peace process requires the Arab nation to stand firm and not to give up its rights in land and security because peace that is based on giving up (this) is rejected even if Israel freezes (peace) talks for many years".

Palestinian-Israeli ties deteriorated after Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered the building of a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem, which Palestinians want as the capital of a future state.
The housing scheme has sparked 11 days of clashes and last week an Islamist suicide bomber killed three Israelis in Tel Aviv.
The UAE and its Gulf allies have condemned the settlement and many Arab and Islamic countries said that they would reconsider their ties with Israel unless it stopped construction work.
The UAE cabinet has 23 ministers, two fewer than the outgoing cabinet. The ministries of justice and Islamic affairs were merged, as were the education and youth and sports ministries.
The former cabinet, appointed in November 1990 following the death of Sheikh Rashid bin Said al-Maktoum, father of the prime minister and vice-president, resigned on March 16.
Since 1990, several ministers had been changed but this was the first major reshuffle in the Gulf state, a member of the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC).

The highest federal authority in the UAE, where there are no political parties, is the Supreme Council composed of the rulers of the seven emirates. The Federal National Council, appointed by the rulers, has a consultative role.
